title: A Pacific temperature contrast cut six-month volume forecast error by 12.63% beyond twelve-month history in 2000-2023
abstract: We tested whether an east-west Pacific temperature contrast adds six-month warm water volume forecast information beyond a full year of volume and Nino 3.4 history. We used fixed NOAA GODAS and CPC ERSSTv5 records. Annual expanding fits and inner chronological forecasts chose ridge penalties using earlier completed targets only. At 288 monthly origins in 2000-2023, current and six-month past Nino 3 minus Nino 4 reduced mean squared error by 12.63%. RMSE fell from 0.81271 to 0.75965 in units of 10^14 cubic metres. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was 3.28% to 23.02%. The one-year block interval included zero. Six- and twenty-four-month history checks retained positive three-year limits. Thus, these longer histories did not remove the spatial contrast gain within the tested ridge models. This extends prior work on the same data and is not independent confirmation. Revised records, fixed anomaly bases, few cycles, model choice, release timing and conditional uncertainty limit inference. No physical cause or operational forecast skill is established. The package gives original code, aggregate scores, all tuning scores, source hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Added temperature contrast reduced six-month volume forecast error beyond 6, 12 and 24 past monthly lags. Bars show conditional 95% three-year score-block limits. The primary twelve-lag one-year interval includes zero. Right: annual squared errors for the primary models.
